summary: RFC 4412 defines the Resource-Priority Namespaces and Priority-values registries with a management policy of Standards Action. This document updates RFC 4412 to change that policy to IETF Review.

eli5.summary: A club decided that getting a new entry on its list should be a bit easier. This lowers the bar for adding entries to those lists.

questions: ietf review for sip resource priority namespaces
what is ietf review for sip resource priority
subtitle: Makes it easier to register new Resource-Priority namespaces by switching to IETF Review.

tldr.problem: The Resource-Priority registries required Standards Action, which forced a Standards Track document even for a new namespace that adds no protocol semantics.
tldr.mechanism: The management policy of the Resource-Priority Namespaces and Priority-values registries changes to IETF Review.
tldr.outcome: A document that only defines a namespace and its priorities no longer has to be Standards Track.

today: RFC 7134 is a Proposed Standard from March 2014 that updates RFC 4412. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 4412 defines the "Resource-Priority Namespaces" and "Resource-Priority Priority-values" registries, managed under "Standards Action". Experience suggests that a document that only defines a new namespace with its priorities, and creates no new protocol semantics, should not be a Standards Track document.
sections.eli5: The rules for adding to the list were stricter than they needed to be.

sections.title: The Policy Change
sections.content:
This document updates RFC 4412 to change the management policy of both registries to "IETF Review" (RFC 5226).

IANA has made that change to the "Resource-Priority Namespaces" and "Resource-Priority Priority-values" registries.
sections.eli5: Now the rule for adding to the list is a little looser.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: This document does not introduce any security considerations beyond those discussed in RFC 4412.
sections.eli5: Nothing new is risky, because only the paperwork rule changed.
